title: Citation (engage-lexicon)
description: Required shape of every citation entry produced by an engage-lexicon subagent report. Forked from /debate-prism's citation-schema.json (#214) and extended with legal-domain fields: jurisdiction, courtLevel, year, pinCite, authorityType (the source-class enum specialized for legal authority), authorityWeight (the controlling-vs-persuasive distinction). Every non-derived claim in a report must point at one of these.

title.description: Human-readable title of the authority (case caption, statute short title, regulation name, agency guidance name, treatise title).

url.description: Absolute URL of the canonical or authoritative source. Must be http(s). Prefer official sources (court reporters, agency websites, Cornell LII, GovInfo) over aggregators.

fetchedAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when the source was retrieved via WebFetch/WebSearch. Must include timezone.

excerpt.description: Short quoted or paraphrased extract from the source that supports the claim. Paraphrases must stay true to the source; do not fabricate text. For case citations, prefer the holding language; for statutes, prefer the operative text.

jurisdiction.description: The jurisdiction this authority controls in. Examples: 'US-Federal', 'US-CA', 'US-CA-9th', 'US-NY-SDNY', 'US-DE-Chancery', 'EU', 'EU-Germany', 'UK', 'CA-Ontario'. Matches the format declared via --jurisdiction. For authorities cited as persuasive across forum lines, this field is the authority's OWN controlling jurisdiction (not the forum the claim is in).

courtLevel.description: Court level for case citations. Use 'not-applicable' for statutes, regulations, agency guidance, secondary sources. 'specialty-court' covers tax court, bankruptcy court, ITC, etc. 'supranational' covers ECJ, ICJ, WTO panels.

year.description: The year the authority was issued, enacted, or most recently amended in the form the advocate is relying on. For cases, the decision year; for statutes/regulations, the version year (the recency gate compares this to the most-recent-amendment date).

pinCite.description: Optional. Pin cite within the authority. For cases: page/paragraph number within the opinion (e.g., '485 U.S. 224, 232'). For statutes: subsection (e.g., '15 U.S.C. § 78j(b)'). For regulations: paragraph (e.g., '17 C.F.R. § 240.10b-5(b)'). Pin cites strengthen citations; absence is acceptable when the entire authority is being cited.

authorityType.description: Source-class enum specialized for legal authority. The hierarchy from highest authority to lowest (within a declared jurisdiction): constitutional-provision > statute > regulation > controlling-case > agency-guidance > persuasive-case > treaty (varies) > restatement > treatise > law-review > bar-publication > amicus-brief > news > other. 'controlling-case' = binding precedent in the cited jurisdiction; 'persuasive-case' = out-of-jurisdiction or dicta. Authority-hierarchy diversity gate (#202 AC5) uses this enum together with authorityWeight.

authorityWeight.description: The controlling-vs-persuasive distinction (#202 AC6, AC5). 'controlling' = binding on the forum (statute applicable in jurisdiction, regulation applicable in jurisdiction, case from a court whose decisions bind the forum, treaty in force in jurisdiction with self-executing provisions). 'persuasive' = informative but not binding (out-of-jurisdiction cases, secondary sources, dicta, withdrawn guidance, non-self-executing treaty provisions, foreign case law cited for analogy). This distinction is what separates 'the Ninth Circuit decided X' from 'the Supreme Court decided X' in citation weight; the judge MUST annotate every cited authority with this field.

author.description: Optional. Author of the opinion (judge), drafter (statute), agency (regulation/guidance), or commentator (secondary source).

publishedAt.description: Optional. ISO-8601 publication date (case decision date, statute enactment date, regulation final-rule date, agency guidance issuance date, article publication date). Used by the recency gate.

mostRecentAmendmentDate.description: Optional but recommended for authorityType in {statute, regulation, agency-guidance}. ISO-8601 date of the most recent amendment, repeal, or supersession that affects this authority. Used by the statutory recency gate (Step 6) — when this date is significantly after `year`, the citation is flagged statutoryRecencyStale and the judge must assess materiality.

supersededBy.description: Optional. If this authority has been superseded (case overruled, statute repealed and re-enacted, regulation withdrawn and re-issued), the canonical citation of the superseding authority. Use sparingly — only when the advocate is intentionally citing the superseded form for historical analysis.

urlUnreachable.description: Optional. Set true when the URL was valid at citation time but is no longer reachable. Do not invent an alternative.
